meta: Demo quiz bank for RoadSafe AI. Every question links to a corpus section id (or the Punjab signs guide). Answers must be verified against official law before any commercial use.

questions.q: A steady red traffic light means…
options: Stop behind the stop line and wait for green
Stop, then carefully turn right immediately
Slow down and proceed if no traffic
questions.explanation: Red means stop before the line; turning on red is not allowed unless a sign permits it.

questions.q: A steady amber (yellow) light means…
options: Speed up to clear the junction
Stop before the line if safe; otherwise clear with care
questions.explanation: Amber warns the light is about to turn red — stop if you can do so safely.

questions.q: On a steady green light you must still…
options: Give way to pedestrians on the crossing and traffic already in the junction
questions.explanation: Green means proceed with care, not blindly — crossings and vehicles inside the junction have priority.

questions.q: A flashing red light at night should be treated as…
options: A stop sign: full stop, yield, then go when safe
questions.explanation: Flashing red = complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, proceed when safe.

questions.q: A flashing amber light means…
options: Proceed with caution, giving way where needed
The same as a red light
questions.explanation: Flashing amber does not require a stop, but you must slow down and take care.

questions.q: A green right-turn arrow means…
options: You have a protected right turn — conflicting traffic faces red
questions.explanation: A green arrow protects the movement it shows; still yield to pedestrians.

questions.q: The main light is green but the right-turn arrow shows red. You may…
options: Turn right only if no police are watching
Not make that turn — wait for the green arrow
questions.explanation: A red arrow prohibits the movement it points to, even if the main light is green.

questions.q: The pedestrian signal shows a flashing DON'T WALK. A pedestrian should…
options: Not start; finish clearing if already crossing
questions.explanation: Flashing DON'T WALK means don't start — clear the crossing if you're already on it.

questions.q: The signals at a junction are completely off (power failure). You should treat it as…
questions.explanation: Blackout: stop and take turns in order of arrival; follow a traffic officer if present.

questions.q: A traffic warden's hand signals contradict the lights. You should…
questions.explanation: A traffic officer on duty overrides the signals.

questions.q: You approach a green light but traffic ahead is gridlocked across the junction. You should…
options: Wait behind the line until you can fully clear
questions.explanation: Keep clear — don't enter a junction you cannot exit, even on green.

questions.q: At an unsignalized junction you should yield primarily to…
options: Traffic approaching from your right and vehicles already in the junction
questions.explanation: Yield to the vehicle on your right and whoever is already in the junction.

questions.q: Where must you stop at a red light?
options: Behind the white stop line (or before the crossing)
questions.explanation: Stop behind the stop line — never inside the junction or on the zebra.

questions.q: An amber light appears and you are 2 metres from the line at 50 km/h. You should…
options: Continue through with caution — you cannot stop safely
questions.explanation: If stopping safely is impossible, clear the junction without accelerating.

questions.q: Night flash: main road shows flashing amber, side road flashing red. You are on the side road. You…
options: Must stop, yield to the main road, then go when safe
questions.explanation: Flashing red side road = stop and yield; flashing amber main road = caution.

questions.q: A steady red pedestrian man (DON'T WALK) means pedestrians…
questions.explanation: Steady DON'T WALK = do not enter the crossing.

questions.q: During an all-red clearance phase you should…
questions.explanation: All-red phases exist to clear the junction — remain stopped.

questions.q: Red-light cameras flash as you enter on amber having safely cleared. This is…
options: Permitted if you could not stop safely — amber means clear with care
questions.explanation: Entering on amber to clear safely is not red-light jumping; crossing on red is.

questions.q: A green light plus a green right-arrow simultaneously means…
options: Straight traffic AND protected right turns both move
questions.explanation: Arrows add a protected movement on top of the main green.

questions.q: Traffic signals exist primarily to…
options: Allocate right of way in turn and reduce conflict points
questions.explanation: Signals serialise conflicting movements — predictability saves lives.

questions.q: In Pakistan, traffic at a roundabout circulates…
questions.explanation: Left-hand-traffic rules: roundabout flow is clockwise.

questions.q: Before entering a roundabout you must yield to…
options: Traffic already on the roundabout coming from your right
questions.explanation: Those already circulating from your right have priority.

questions.q: Inside a roundabout you should…
options: Keep moving and signal before your exit
Reverse if you miss the exit
Stop for photos of the monument
questions.explanation: Never stop inside; signal your exit so followers can predict you.

questions.q: For the FIRST exit at a roundabout (left-hand traffic), the best lane is…
questions.explanation: Earlier (first) exits are taken from the left lane; later exits from nearer the inside.

questions.q: A truck is using the full width of the roundabout. You should…
questions.explanation: Long vehicles may swing wide — give them space.

questions.q: You miss your intended exit at a roundabout. You should…
options: Continue around and take it on the next pass
questions.explanation: Go around again — never reverse or stop inside.

questions.q: An eight-sided (octagonal) sign reading STOP means…
options: Come to a complete stop, then proceed when safe
questions.explanation: The octagon is the stop sign — full stop required.

questions.q: An inverted (upside-down) triangle sign means…
questions.explanation: The inverted triangle is the yield sign — give priority to the major road.

questions.q: A red circle with a number (e.g. 60) means…
questions.explanation: A number in a red ring is a mandatory maximum speed.

questions.q: A red circle with a white horizontal bar means…
questions.explanation: The 'no entry' sign — you must not enter that road.

questions.q: A blue circle sign generally indicates…
questions.explanation: Blue circles give compulsory instructions like keep left or turn right.

questions.q: Red-bordered triangle signs are used for…
questions.explanation: Triangles warn: junction, school, cattle, slippery road, etc.

questions.q: A rectangular blue sign typically gives…
questions.explanation: Blue rectangles inform; green rectangles give directions.

questions.q: A yellow kerb line means…
questions.explanation: Yellow kerb marking = no stopping/parking along that stretch.

questions.q: At road works, the temporary signs and cones…
options: Can be ignored if you know the road
questions.explanation: Temporary controls take precedence; comply with reduced limits.

questions.q: Zebra stripes across the road mark…
questions.explanation: Zebras give pedestrians priority — slow and give way.

questions.q: A school warning triangle appears. You should…
options: Reduce speed well below the limit and never overtake
questions.explanation: School zones demand extra care: slow down, no overtaking, be ready to stop.

questions.q: Arrows painted on your lane show straight-only. You may…
options: Only continue straight — change lanes earlier to turn
questions.explanation: Lane arrows prescribe permitted movements; pick the correct lane in advance.

questions.q: A 'no overtaking' sign (red ring, two cars) means…
options: Do not overtake until the sign cancels it
questions.explanation: The prohibition applies until a cancellation sign.

questions.q: A roundabout-ahead warning triangle tells you to…
options: Expect a roundabout shortly — slow and prepare to yield
questions.explanation: Warning signs give advance notice — adjust speed early.

questions.q: Which sign shape is NEVER used for warnings?
questions.explanation: The octagon is reserved exclusively for STOP.

questions.q: Chevron alignment signs (white arrows on a panel) mark…
options: A sharp bend or hazard edge to follow the road
questions.explanation: Chevrons trace the line of a sharp curve — follow them, slow down.

questions.q: A 'no horn' sign means…
options: Do not sound the horn in this zone (often near hospitals)
questions.explanation: Silence zones (hospitals, schools) prohibit horn use.

questions.q: Ignoring a regulatory sign (e.g. entering 'no entry') is…
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are legally binding on all vehicles.

questions.q: The motorway maximum speed for light cars is…
questions.explanation: Motorway max for cars is 120 km/h; heavier vehicles have lower limits.

questions.q: The motorway MINIMUM speed (light vehicles) is…
questions.explanation: Below 60 km/h you must not use the motorway.

questions.q: In Pakistan you normally drive…
options: On the left side of the road
questions.explanation: Pakistan keeps left; the right side is for overtaking.

questions.q: The hard shoulder on a motorway may be used…
options: As a normal lane in traffic jams
questions.explanation: Shoulder = emergencies only; driving on it is an offence.

questions.q: A safe following distance in good conditions is at least…
questions.explanation: Use the 3-second rule; double it in rain or low grip.

questions.q: Where no limit is posted, your speed should allow you to…
options: Stop within the distance you can see to be clear
questions.explanation: The classic rule: be able to stop in your visible clear distance.

questions.q: After overtaking on the motorway you should…
options: Return to the left lane when safely clear
Brake hard in front of the truck
questions.explanation: Keep left except to overtake — return once clear.

questions.q: In fog, the motorway advisory is to…
options: Use high beams and follow close
Reduce speed, use low beams/fog lamps, increase gap, follow signs
Drive on the shoulder with hazards
questions.explanation: High beams reflect back off fog; the gap is your braking distance.

questions.q: You miss your motorway exit. You should…
options: Stop and wait for a gap
questions.explanation: Reversing or crossing the median on a motorway is prohibited and lethal.

questions.q: Overtaking on the motorway from the LEFT is…
questions.explanation: Pass on the right; left-side passing is prohibited on the motorway.

questions.q: Approaching a school zone, you should…
options: Slow well below the limit and watch for children
questions.explanation: Children behave unpredictably — the posted/zone speed applies.

questions.q: In heavy rain your following distance should be…
questions.explanation: Wet roads can double stopping distance — double the gap.

questions.q: You should overtake another vehicle…
options: On its right, when the way is clearly visible
questions.explanation: Overtake on the right with full visibility — never at junctions or crossings.

questions.q: Where is overtaking prohibited?
options: Junctions, pedestrian crossings, bridges, curves and crests
questions.explanation: All of these hide conflicts — overtake elsewhere.

questions.q: The driver being overtaken should…
options: Hold speed and stay left, allowing the pass
questions.explanation: Speeding up while being overtaken is an offence.

questions.q: Before changing lanes you should…
options: Signal, check mirrors and blind spot, then move
questions.explanation: MSM: Mirror–Signal–Manoeuvre.

questions.q: Turning RIGHT across oncoming traffic you must…
options: Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
questions.explanation: The right turn crosses opposing flow — oncoming traffic has priority.

questions.q: A U-turn is…
options: Allowed only where not prohibited and safe
questions.explanation: U-turn where permitted, safe, and clearly visible; never on the motorway.

questions.q: Turning on red (any direction) in Pakistan is…
options: Not permitted unless a sign expressly allows it
questions.explanation: Red means stop; turns on red require an explicit sign.

questions.q: You are being overtaken and a pedestrian appears ahead. You should…
options: Speed up to finish the pass
Ease off to let the overtaking driver back in safely
questions.explanation: Cooperate — create space for the passer to return to the lane.

questions.q: Reversing on a motorway to recover a missed exit is…
questions.explanation: Never reverse on a motorway — continue to the next interchange.

questions.q: Signalling a turn should happen…
questions.explanation: Early signals give others time to react.

questions.q: Minimum age for a car driving licence (general rule)…
questions.explanation: 18 for cars/motorcycles; learners need a permit and an 'L' plate.

questions.q: A learner driver…
options: Must hold a learner permit, display 'L', and not drive alone
questions.explanation: Learners: permit + L-plate + supervision; motorway use is prohibited.

questions.q: Which documents should be available when driving?
questions.explanation: Producing licence, registration and insurance on demand is required.

questions.q: The minimum mandatory insurance cover is…
questions.explanation: At least third-party cover is legally required.

questions.q: Who may NOT use the motorway?
questions.explanation: Learners, non-motorised traffic and pedestrians are barred.

questions.q: Driving without a valid licence is…
options: An offence — vehicle may be impounded
questions.explanation: No valid licence = offence; police may impound.

questions.q: A pillion passenger on a motorcycle…
questions.explanation: At most one pillion; overload is an offence.

questions.q: Driving while unfit due to alcohol or drugs is…
questions.explanation: Pakistan applies zero tolerance; refusing a test is also an offence.

questions.q: Registration certificate of the vehicle must be…
questions.explanation: It is one of the three core documents to produce.

questions.q: Hand-held mobile phone use while driving is…
options: Prohibited — use hands-free or park first
questions.explanation: No handheld use while moving; park safely with engine off.

questions.q: At a zebra crossing the priority belongs to…
questions.explanation: Slow, and give way to pedestrians already on the zebra.

questions.q: Overtaking a vehicle stopped at a pedestrian crossing is…
questions.explanation: It may be stopped for pedestrians you cannot yet see.

questions.q: When passing a cyclist you should leave…
options: A wide margin (about 1 metre or more)
questions.explanation: Give riders room; a wobble or pothole can throw them into your path.

questions.q: Pedestrians on the motorway are…
questions.explanation: No pedestrians on motorways at all.

questions.q: The pedestrian WALK signal starts flashing as you approach the kerb. You should…
questions.explanation: Don't start on flashing DON'T WALK — wait for the next phase.

questions.q: Animal-drawn carts on the highway are…
options: Faster than expected — overtake blind corners anyway
Slow and unpredictable — pass wide and patiently
questions.explanation: Expect sudden moves; give slow traffic wide, patient clearance.

questions.q: Children near the roadway require drivers to…
options: Slow and be ready to stop at any moment
questions.explanation: Especially near schools — expect the unexpected.

questions.q: A motorcycle rider and pillion must both…
questions.explanation: Helmets are mandatory for rider AND pillion.

questions.q: Parking at a pedestrian crossing or junction is…
questions.explanation: Never stop or park at crossings, junctions, bridges or tunnels.

questions.q: Double parking (beside a parked car) is…
questions.explanation: Double parking obstructs and endangers everyone.

questions.q: Stopping on a motorway carriageway is…
options: Prohibited — use lay-bys or the hard shoulder in emergencies only
questions.explanation: Never stop on the carriageway; emergencies go to the shoulder.

questions.q: Broken down on the motorway: after moving to the shoulder you should…
options: Hazard lights on, warning triangle ~100 m back, wait behind the barrier, call 130/1122
Stand in front of the car
questions.explanation: Get behind the barrier — motorway traffic kills at distance.

questions.q: A yellow line at the kerb indicates…
questions.explanation: Yellow kerb = no stopping.

questions.q: Using hazard lights while DRIVING in normal rain is…
options: Wrong — hazards are for stationary/broken-down vehicles
questions.explanation: Hazards while moving cancel your indicators and confuse others.

questions.q: Parking on a footpath is…
options: Prohibited — it forces pedestrians into traffic
questions.explanation: Footpaths are for pedestrians — blocking them endangers lives.

questions.q: Before leaving a parallel-parked car you should…
options: Open the door fully to stretch
Check mirrors and open the door with the far hand, watching for bikes
questions.explanation: 'Dutch reach' — doorings seriously injure motorcyclists.

questions.q: In dense fog on the motorway, high-beam headlights are…
options: Harmful — light reflects back and reduces visibility
questions.explanation: Use low beams + fog lamps; high beams bounce back off the fog.

questions.q: In fog your speed should be…
options: Well below the limit with a bigger gap
As fast as possible to exit the fog
questions.explanation: Reduce speed and multiply the gap — your vision is your stopping distance.

questions.q: If the Motorway Police announce a convoy/escort in fog, you should…
questions.explanation: Escorts move in guided groups — following is the safe protocol.

questions.q: Night driving on an UNLIT rural road, oncoming lights blind you. You should…
options: Look to the left edge of your lane, slow down
questions.explanation: Avoid the glare source, keep lane reference, reduce speed.

questions.q: The road is wet after the first rain of the season. The biggest hidden danger is…
options: Slick oil/dust film and longer braking — slow down
questions.explanation: First rain lifts oil and dust: grip drops sharply.

questions.q: Your car starts aquaplaning (tyres floating on water). You should…
options: Ease off the accelerator, hold steering straight, let it settle
questions.explanation: Sudden inputs cause a spin; decelerate gently until grip returns.

questions.q: A dust storm reduces visibility to metres. You should…
options: Pull over safely off the road, lights on, wait it out
questions.explanation: If you cannot see, get off the carriageway and wait.

questions.q: Long motorway journeys: take a rest break at least…
questions.explanation: Rest every two hours — drowsy driving kills like alcohol.

questions.q: After a collision your FIRST duties are…
options: Stop, help the injured, exchange details, report to police
questions.explanation: Stop and render aid — leaving is a serious offence.

questions.q: The ambulance/medical emergency number in Punjab is…
questions.explanation: Rescue 1122 handles medical emergencies; 15 is police, 130 motorway police.

questions.q: A casualty with a suspected spinal injury should be…
options: Left in place unless there is greater danger; call 1122
questions.explanation: Moving them can worsen the injury — protect the scene and call help.

questions.q: Breakdown on the motorway — which helpline is dedicated to the Motorway Police?
questions.explanation: 130 reaches NHMP; 1122 for medical rescue.

questions.q: To protect a crash scene at night you should…
options: Use hazard lights and a warning triangle to warn traffic
questions.explanation: Secondary collisions are a major killer — warn oncoming traffic early.

questions.q: Reporting an accident to police should happen…
questions.explanation: Report as soon as practicable; failing to report is an offence.
